      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/19/baobab-five-trees-south-africa-dug-up-export-blocked-georgia-aoe</link>
      <description><p>The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits</p><p>Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.</p><p>The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/19/baobab-five-trees-south-africa-dug-up-export-blocked-georgia-aoe">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/women-girls-rights-rape-sexual-violence-africa-marriage-unfpa</link>
      <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/race-to-be-next-un-secretary-general-exposes-divisions-among-world-powers</link>
      <description><p>Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner</p><p>The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations.</p><p>Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/race-to-be-next-un-secretary-general-exposes-divisions-among-world-powers">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘So what if there’s a hole? It hasn’t collapsed’: Kyiv residents unbothered by Russian attacks on city’s bridges</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/21/kyiv-russian-attacks-bridges</link>
      <description><p>Despite dodging tears in the tarmac, people are confident in city’s infrastructure – and will not worry about what has not happened yet</p><p>Mykola expects to drive his battered beige passenger minibus 20 to 24 times a day past the holes in the road on Kyiv’s damaged Northern Bridge that were caused by a Russian ballistic missile attack on Tuesday.</p><p>Buses are now the only motor transport allowed across the normally busy multi-lane crossing, though on their way into the city centre they have to skirt the tears in the tarmac, using the only functioning lane to get by.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/21/kyiv-russian-attacks-bridges">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Tourists are throwing fewer coins into Rome’s Trevi fountain – is €2 entry fee to blame?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/21/charity-hit-coin-throwing-rome-trevi-fountain-caritas-italy</link>
      <description><p>Charity that collects the coins says donations are down by £200,000 after a barrier was put in place to restrict access</p><p>When Jeff Clinton, an American visiting Rome with his wife for the first time, found a US one-cent coin on a street close to Termini train station, he knew precisely what he was going to do with it. “I’ll throw it into the Trevi fountain,” said Clinton, holding the copper coin in the palm of his hand as the couple admired the landmark.</p><p>He was well aware of the tradition among tourists of tossing a coin over their shoulder and into the waters of the baroque masterpiece, in a ritual fabled to ensure a return visit to the city or make other dreams come true.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/21/charity-hit-coin-throwing-rome-trevi-fountain-caritas-italy">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/french-police-officers-found-guilty-of-racist-assault-on-black-music-producer</link>
      <description><p>Beating of Michel Zecler in 2020 sparked outrage over police brutality after it was caught on security cameras</p><p>Three French police officers who beat a black music producer they said was not wearing a face mask during the Covid pandemic have been found guilty of intentional, racist violence.</p><p>The <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/09/french-police-officers-face-trial-over-beating-of-black-man-not-wearing-mask-during-covid">brutal assault</a> on Michel Zecler, now 47, was caught on security cameras in his building in 2020 and triggered outrage in France over police brutality. The trial this month was considered a turning point for the recognition of racist violence.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/french-police-officers-found-guilty-of-racist-assault-on-black-music-producer">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Spain frees wealthy US-sought activist on bail as Irish police raid Dublin home</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/james-fergie-chambers-bail-spain</link>
      <description><p>Pro-Palestinian donor James ‘Fergie’ Chambers released as court considers extradition request</p><p>In a blur of events surrounding the Trump administration’s effort to extradite James “Fergie” Chambers, Spain released the wealthy US activist and donor on bail even as Irish police raided a Dublin house owned by Chambers and his partner, Stella Schnabel, acting on a request from US authorities.</p><p>Chambers’s case is the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jul/18/fergie-chambers-stella-schnabel-spain-extradition">first known instance</a> of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money-laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/james-fergie-chambers-bail-spain">Continue reading...</a></description>

The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 22:23:26 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>French Greens candidate gives hard-left Mélenchon a boost in presidential race</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-french-greens-candidate-gives-hard-left-melenchon-a-boost-in-presidential-race</link><description>
French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has said an alliance with the Greens "should be possible", after the head of the Greens tentatively agreed to back him, angering moderates on the centre-left. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">40b0fb0e-e4dc-11f1-a123-31d05317ef57</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:04:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg">© REUTERS - Tom Nicholson </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Depardieu and Houellebecq accused of gang rape on French film set</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-depardieu-and-houellebecq-accused-of-gang-rape-on-french-film-set</link><description>
Paris prosecutors have opened an investigation after an actress filed a complaint alleging that she was raped by a group including actor Gérard Depardieu and high-profile French author Michel Houellebecq on the set of the film Thalasso in 2018. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ec3acb0c-e4dd-11f1-9619-3935a39ed096</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:24:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg">REUTERS - Gonzalo Fuentes</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France probes suspected leaks from interior ministry to far-right National Rally</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-france-probes-suspected-leaks-from-interior-ministry-to-far-right-national-rally</link><description>
France has opened a probe into suspicions that a senior official at the interior ministry leaked secret information to the far-right National Rally (RN) party, which is itself facing a number of investigations, prosecutors have said.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5be0a25a-e4b2-11f1-be46-714476ef8919</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:55:01 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg">© Pascal Guyot / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French union leader warns strikes will continue without higher wages</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-french-union-leader-warns-strikes-will-continue-without-higher-wages-cgt-sophie-binet-interview</link><description>
French trade unions have promised to call more strikes and demonstrations, arguing that a government proposal to increase the minimum wage fails to address the social crisis that has spurred protests across the country. Sophie Binet, head of the CGT union, says even after six weeks of action, workers and students are more determined than ever to keep up the fight.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">37c8b342-e40f-11f1-a821-bd0c1d2fd9c6</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 06:07:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© REUTERS - Sarah Meyssonnier </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight on France</category><title>Podcast: Living on the breadline, France's 35-hour week and a divisive tax</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/podcasts/spotlight-on-france/20261119-podcast-living-on-minimum-wage-smic-35-hour-working-week-france-second-biggest-tax-csg</link><description>
The French government's decision to raise the minimum wage has failed to satisfy protesters struggling to make ends meet amid the cost-of-living crisis. Also, did the introduction of the 35-hour working week actually help reduce unemployment? The evidence is mixed. And a look at the history of France's second-largest tax, the CSG, and why it's dividing politicians. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8a275ba4-e41c-11f1-8716-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-153-light-blue.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8a275ba4-e41c-11f1-8716-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-153-light-blue.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">da07160a-e41c-11f1-9424-dd481487d627</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:19:04 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sarah Elzas</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France raises bird flu alert to highest level as infections spread across Europe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261119-france-raises-bird-flu-alert-to-highest-level-as-infections-spread-across-europe</link><description>
France is raising its avian flu alert to the highest level from Friday, bringing new restrictions on poultry movements as authorities seek to contain the spread of the virus. The decision comes amid a rise in infections among wild birds across Europe, particularly along migration routes crossing France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eff2afda-e3f7-11f1-a0c0-bdb47d3d53b3</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:12:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png">© GAIZKA IROZ / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France rejects 'absurd' Russian claims of direct involvement in Ukraine war</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-france-rejects-absurd-russian-claims-of-direct-involvement-in-ukraine-war</link><description>
The French government on Tuesday dismissed Russian accusations that France is directly involved in the war in Ukraine, following an RFI investigation which revealed a small number of French soldiers have been carrying out training and equipment maintenance missions on Ukrainian territory. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ffdd448e-e346-11f1-831b-65a66bd770f6</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:39:09 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg">AFP - BERTRAND GUAY</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French interior minister accused of 'exaggerating' police protest injury figures</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-french-interior-minister-accused-of-exaggerating-police-protest-injury-figures</link><description>
A group of lawyers have called for an investigation into French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez who they accuse of "spreading false information" about the number of injuries suffered by law enforcement officers since the start of the current protest movement, which they say was used "to justify a disproportionate use of force" against high school protesters.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">294b16e6-e335-11f1-af18-6757e9484dfb</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:09:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg">AFP - SEBASTIEN BOZON</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'We weren't afraid of the future': France's student protests today and in May '68</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-we-weren-t-afraid-of-the-future-france-s-student-protests-today-and-in-may-68</link><description>
As students across France continue demonstrating against conditions in schools, the movement has drawn inevitable comparisons with the biggest student protests in the country's history – those of May 1968. While this date remains a rallying cry for many young French people, they are calling for change in a world that has altered profoundly in the past 58 years.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">457488e8-dceb-11f1-88f8-bd68fc553891</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:01:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg">© JACQUES MARIE / AFP </source><dc:creator>Jessica Phelan</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Lower turnout at latest French cost-of-living protests, but anger still raw</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-lower-turnout-at-latest-french-cost-of-living-protests-but-anger-still-raw</link><description>
Tens of thousands of people demonstrated across France on Tuesday in a fresh nationwide public sector strike over pay and the cost of living. A French anti-cybercrime unit was on Monday investigating a massive cyberattack which targeted a subsidiary of the La Poste group mid-September. The contact details of 22 million people were exposed during the attack, the Paris prosecutor's office confirmed on Sunday.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5343e1a8-dd22-11f1-9ec6-3535b33525c6</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:14:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Stephane Mahe</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>How France's student protests grew into a broader movement amid police violence</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261114-how-france-s-student-protests-grew-into-a-broader-movement-amid-police-violence</link><description>

France faces more rallies on Saturday with demonstrators venting frustrations ranging from inflation, to child protection measures and opposition to a new police bill.

France is marking the 11th anniversary of the November 2015 Paris terrorist attacks on Friday, with commemorations honouring the 130 people killed. This year the Stade de France, one of the sites targeted by the attackers, hosts a sporting event on 13 November for the first time since the tragedy.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f166e312-df75-11f1-adbe-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25317657554123.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f166e312-df75-11f1-adbe-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25317657554123.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a235f704-df5e-11f1-bb2c-85a37d07b862</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:08:48 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f166e312-df75-11f1-adbe-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25317657554123.jpg">AP - Emma Da Silva</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France slams Russian ‘intimidation’ as fresh EU sanctions come into force</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261113-france-slams-russian-intimidation-fedorova-as-fresh-eu-sanctions-come-into-force</link><description>
The European Union will approve more ​sanctions against Russia on Monday, the bulk of which were proposed by France, the country's Minister for European Affairs Benjamin Haddad said on Thursday. France has requested international arrest warrants for three Iranian men over October’s cyberattack on supermarket fridges, while Tehran rejects the allegations as “baseless and malicious”.

French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.

French student leaders on Monday called for more protests despite President Emmanuel Macron's pledge of  "concrete and strong" measures to address their demands after weeks of nationwide unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met with high school representatives alongside education ministers to announce follow-up action ranging from a total overhaul of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup to a cap on class sizes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ade564d2-d134-11f1-9bc8-6d20ccb9a352</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:25:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20210714-how-the-french-army-trains-for-high-intensity-conflict</link><description>
France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">023ce07e-e41d-11eb-a94a-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 14:42:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fadile BHAYAT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says 'racist terrorist attack’ in Trappes marks turning point for France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261023-french-prosecutors-investigate-paris-shooting-as-suspected-terror-attack</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron described Friday’s drive-by shooting in the western suburb of Trappes as a “terrorist and racist attack”, saying it marks a turning point for France. One person was killed and at least four people, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in the shooting, apparently at random. Two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72670cfa-ced0-11f1-8bc7-bb90dbb6a8a1</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:08:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg">© Hannah McKay, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'A lot of French politicians are out of touch with a large part of the population'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20220209-a-lot-of-french-politicians-are-out-of-touch-with-a-large-part-of-the-population</link><description>

French President Emmanuel Macron took aim at world leaders including US President Donald Trump for trying to exploit the riots and looting that broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in France Saturday for their own political advantage. Two teaching staff were shot and wounded by a 14-year-old boy armed with a hunting rifle at a school in Aubagne near Marseille Monday morning, French Education Minister ‌Édouard Geffray said. Authorities said the teenager's father had been taken into custody and that there did not seem to be any link to the student protests that have swept across the country in recent weeks.

As France's April presidential election approaches, the campaign is getting under way in earnest. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">99b61d02-c596-11f1-9bf5-777190d2ada5</guid><pubDate>Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:50:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fire destroys Paris's oldest covered food market</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-fire-burns-down-paris-s-oldest-covered-food-market</link><description>
A fire "completely destroyed" Paris's historic Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges early Monday, authorities said. The cause of the fire that swept through the capital's oldest covered food market remains unknown. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5504c60-c610-11f1-b48e-936bba59cf88</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:02:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg">© Creative Commons</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French police clash with teens blockading schools as unions stage day of protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-french-police-clash-with-teens-blockading-schools-as-union-stage-day-of-protests</link><description>
French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of high schools in cities across the country to demand better conditions and more teacher hirings. The escalating standoff came as unions staged a day of demonstrations against a cost-cutting budget drafted by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's embattled government.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b23ed102-bbeb-11f1-861d-cf265369200f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:53:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-legion-of-honour-police-investigate-corruption-claims-for-france-s-top-award</link><description>
French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <title>Labor leaders call on governments to stop awarding Amazon public contracts</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/labor-unions-amazon-contracts-open-letter</link>
      <description><p>Union leaders from 19 countries urge reassessment of ties to Amazon, citing company’s poor record on worker rights</p><p>More than 30 labor union leaders from 19 countries are calling on governments to review their public contracts with Amazon and Amazon Web Services, citing the company’s poor record on worker rights and collective bargaining, in an<a href="https://uniglobalunion.org/wp-content/uploads/Amazon-procurement-letter-embargoed-until-nov-19.pdf"> open letter</a> published on Thursday.</p><p>“Amazon’s consistent record of disrespect for workers’ fundamental rights should disqualify it from being awarded public contracts – its behaviour is fundamentally inconsistent with the shared democratic values of our countries,” the union leaders wrote.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/labor-unions-amazon-contracts-open-letter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Company issues first earnings report after ouster of CEO over allegations of affair with suspected Chinese spy</p><p>Nvidia “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”, the chairman of the company’s board said Tuesday. Harvey Jones made the remark during Nvidia’s first quarterly earnings report since Jensen Huang’s ouster.</p><p>Nvidia announced the same day that its quarterly revenue beat expectations, coming in at $115.84bn, doubling from the same time period a year ago.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/17/deutsche-bank-dimissed-warnings-risky-clients-reports-claim</link>
      <description><p>International investigation using trove of leaked internal data allegedly shows German bank overlooked compliance concerns to safeguard profits</p><p>Deutsche Bank reportedly dismissed warnings about its dealings with risky clients, including high-profile Russian oligarchs, to protect profits, the findings of an investigation into a trove of leaked bank documents indicate.</p><p>A leak of 15m internal files is reported to show that the troubled German bank repeatedly ignored concerns by its compliance officers about its risk-taking, despite having already <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2019/apr/17/deutsche-bank-faces-action-over-20bn-russian-money-laundering-scheme">been caught being used to launder billions of dollars</a> for Russian criminals, spies and oligarchs between 2010 and 2015.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/17/deutsche-bank-dimissed-warnings-risky-clients-reports-claim">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>When partners consider finances, when is it ‘my’ money, and when it is ‘our’ money?       <description><p>A citizen referendum, only the second of its kind in Georgia history, seeks to block a zoning amendment</p><p>Ire Gene Grovner stood behind his house on a recent morning, between chicken pens on one side and rows of winter collard greens on the other, holding a knife and skinning a raccoon splayed across a wood post.</p><p>“The meat is good roasted,” Grovner said.       <title>Pochettino the connector: will human touch lift Manchester United?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/mauricio-pochettino-manchester-united-manager-liverpool-premier-league</link>
      <description><p>Argentinian has excelled in man-management – but will need his powers to energise new squad and impress owners</p><p>Mauricio Pochettino celebrated his 50th birthday in style. It was March 2022, he was in charge at Paris Saint-Germain and the venue was a stunning boutique hotel; the kind that many capitals have but only Paris truly <em>does</em>. Pochettino’s family and friends were there. So were his inner coaching circle, who are basically family. There were lots of people from PSG. And a good time was had by all.</p><p>For Pochettino, it was emotional. As everybody knows, the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/mauricio-pochettino-arrives-manchester-united-head-coach-premier-league">new Manchester United head coach</a> is the kind of guy to well up when the speeches start, so imagine how he felt when he looked up at the big screen and a video montage of well-wishers started to roll.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/mauricio-pochettino-manchester-united-manager-liverpool-premier-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/dele-alli-tottenham-mk-dons-england</link>
      <description><p>The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player</p><p>Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.</p><p>He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor &amp; Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/dele-alli-tottenham-mk-dons-england">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/washington-spirit-provide-hope-and-joy-in-a-city-that-badly-needs-it</link>
      <description><p>Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than one</p><p>In the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture. In the stands, around 20,000 Spirit supporters had filled the stadium to capacity, the sixth time they’d done so in 2026. They filled the place with the type of wondrous noise that’s become alien in DC sports in recent years, the type of gleeful adoration reserved for the city’s rare winners. The Spirit will return to their home stadium to face the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship this Saturday.</p><p>In short order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/washington-spirit-provide-hope-and-joy-in-a-city-that-badly-needs-it">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/premier-league-table-history-after-10-games-season</link>
      <description><p>Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated</p><p>The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged.</p><p>Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/premier-league-table-history-after-10-games-season">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/premier-league-10-things-to-look-out-for-this-weekend</link>
      <description><p>Bruno Guimarães to feel the heat on Tyneside, Alex Scott’s return further cheers Cherries and Manchester City face favourite whipping boys</p><p>After three Premier League defeats on the spin, Manchester City need something or someone to come along and put some pep in their step, and Fulham look like just the thing – after all, in the past 15 years these teams have played 20 times in all competitions, and City have won precisely 20 of those games. Their current run of 17 successive league wins against Fulham is the longest run of victories by one club against a single opponent in English top-flight history. It is a reflection of the changing realities of English football, and the gulf that has opened between the teams that dominate it and those who seek to challenge them, that of the top 10 such runs all but one occurred in whole or in part after 2010 and six of them have been achieved by Sheikh Mansour’s Manchester City, with Chelsea responsible for another two, Manchester United one, and Portsmouth’s postwar, 13-game supremacy over Everton – a wild ride that included two 5-0s, a 5-1, a 6-3 and a 7-0 – the anomaly. <strong>Simon Burnton</strong></p><p><em>Manchester City v Fulham, Saturday 12.30pm (all times GMT)</em></p><p><em>Aston Villa v Sunderland, Saturday 3pm</em></p><p><em>Bournemouth v Nottingham Forest, Saturday 3pm</em></p><p><em>Chelsea v Leeds</em><em>, Saturday 3pm</em></p><p><em>Coventry v Crystal Palace, Saturday 3pm</em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/premier-league-10-things-to-look-out-for-this-weekend">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>England get one-match suspended ban on away tickets for anti-pope chants in Spain</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/england-one-match-suspended-away-tickets-ban-anti-pope-chants-spain-uefa</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Ban by Uefa is suspended for two years</p></li><li><p>Uefa also fines FA £12,500 for offensive chants</p></li></ul><p>England have been handed a ­suspended ­one-match ban on away ticket sales by Uefa in relation to “­racist and/or ­discriminatory” behaviour by fans at Sunday’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/spain-england-nations-league-match-report">3-2 Nations League victory</a> over Spain. The punishment is suspended for two years.</p><p>Uefa has also fined the Football Association €15,000 (£12,500), with the behaviour in question believed to be the chant of “Fuck the pope and the IRA” at the ­Metropolitano ­Stadium in Madrid. A further charge&nbsp;in the next two years could trigger a ban on away fans for a competitive game.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/england-one-match-suspended-away-tickets-ban-anti-pope-chants-spain-uefa">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/gonzalo-garcia-fulham-spain-premier-leaue-interview</link>
      <description><p>Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham</p><p>The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one.</p><p>Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/gonzalo-garcia-fulham-spain-premier-leaue-interview">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Summer signings join Lionel Messi among MLS’s top earners: Takeaways from the league’s salary release</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/mls-salary-release-lionel-messi-spent-per-point</link>
      <description><p>How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight</p><p>Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m.</p><p>Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/mls-salary-release-lionel-messi-spent-per-point">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘When I walked for Burberry I met Kanye West’: the two lives of Bromley footballer Omar Sowunmi</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/omar-sowunmi-bromley-footballer-model-kanye-west</link>
      <description><p>Full-time defender and part-time model, the 31-year-old is happy to shine a light on both sides of his dual career</p><p>“I was walking down the street one day and someone came up to me and said: ‘I think you should be a model,’” the Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi says. He was already living out many people’s dreams as a professional footballer but was able to assume an alter ego in the world of fashion. There are few parallels between the grind of lower-league football and Milan fashion week but the 31-year-old is adept in both worlds.</p><p>Sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris. On Saturday Bromley travel to Reading under their new manager, Karl Robinson, as they attempt to move off the bottom of League One and the centre-back is clear where his focus lies even after his chance encounter with a model agency employee expanded his horizons.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/omar-sowunmi-bromley-footballer-model-kanye-west">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/syria-womens-football</link>
      <description><p>A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty</p><p>In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close.</p><p>Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/syria-womens-football">Continue reading...</a></description>

Selon les révélations de nos confrères de RFI, des soldats français sont présents sur le sol ukrainien. Cela signifie-t-il que la France est en guerre contre la Russie? Le Général Michel Yakovleff nous donne son point de vue. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e9c4d03a-e52c-11f1-858f-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261120-213009-214054-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e9c4d03a-e52c-11f1-858f-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261120-213009-214054-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b98b6c1a-e538-11f1-9624-dbe97cd0cd66</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 23:18:41 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marion GAUDIN</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Procès Zecler : les trois policiers condamnés à des peines de un à deux ans de prison ferme</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-proc%C3%A8s-zecler-les-trois-policiers-condamn%C3%A9s-%C3%A0-des-peines-de-un-%C3%A0-deux-ans-de-prison-ferme</link><description>
Les trois policiers ayant passé à tabac le producteur de musique noir Michel Zecler en 2020 ont été condamnés à des peines de un à deux ans de prison ferme. L'accusation avait de son côté requis, jeudi, entre quatre et six ans de prison ferme.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">844245cc-e52b-11f1-ab61-a5c9daa303ca</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 21:54:13 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg">© Benoit PEYRUCQ / AFP/Archives</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Journal de l'Afrique</category><title>Guinée/Burkina Faso: tensions après la diffusion de caricatures de M. Doumbouya</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/journal-de-l-afrique/20261120-guin%C3%A9e-burkina-faso-tensions-apr%C3%A8s-la-diffusion-de-caricatures-de-m-doumbouya</link><description>
Les tensions montent entre la Guinée et le Burkina Faso. Conakry vient de couper le signal de la RTB, la télévision publique burkinabè. En cause : un éditorial critique, avec une caricature du président Mamadi Doumbouya. Mais l'affaire va bien au-delà de la télé : elle éclate en pleine répression contre l'orpaillage illégal en Guinée, qui a déjà forcé des dizaines de milliers de Burkinabè à rentrer au pays.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/bb8d961c-e526-11f1-9b09-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/DL00016523-VOD-00044995-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/bb8d961c-e526-11f1-9b09-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/DL00016523-VOD-00044995-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ff8d42dc-e52a-11f1-ab4e-9709edc1e6bd</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 21:40:25 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Kalidou SY</dc:creator></item><item><category>Info ou intox</category><title>Valise nucléaire de Poutine : la mise en scène calculée du Kremlin</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/info-ou-intox/20261120-valise-nucl%C3%A9aire-de-poutine-la-mise-en-sc%C3%A8ne-calcul%C3%A9e-du-kremlin</link><description>
Une vidéo largement relayée ces deux derniers jours montre l’aide de camp de Vladimir Poutine porter la valise nucléaire en marge de la rencontre trilatérale en Chine. Une séquence authentique mise en avant par la Russie pour menacer directement les alliés de l’Ukraine.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d392d93c-e528-11f1-b040-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/Francais-2026-11-20T21-04-10-537Z.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d392d93c-e528-11f1-b040-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/Francais-2026-11-20T21-04-10-537Z.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cd4ab3e6-e529-11f1-8e6a-05b2b01d8875</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 21:31:51 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marc PAUPE</dc:creator></item><item><category>Au cœur de l’info, l’invité</category><title>Johann Chapoutot : "la dédiabolisation du RN est véritablement un mythe"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/au-c%C5%93ur-de-l-info-l-invit%C3%A9/20261120-johann-chapoutot-la-d%C3%A9diabolisation-du-rn-est-v%C3%A9ritablement-un-mythe</link><description>
A 5 mois de la présidentielle en France, le RN domine toujours dans les sondages. Longtemps considéré comme anti républicain, infréquentable, il est désormais aux portes du pouvoir. Comment comprendre cette progression? Quelle est la responsabilité de la classe politique dans cette évolution? Quelles conséquences sur notre démocratie? Johann Chapoutot, Professeur d'Histoire contemporaine, auteur de "La bascule, Allemagne 1933" (éditions Gallimard), était l'Invité d'Au Coeur de l'Info. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20054536-e522-11f1-9d9f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261120-200854-202823-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20054536-e522-11f1-9d9f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261120-200854-202823-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">141cd51a-e525-11f1-8891-754dc11be848</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 20:58:03 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Achren VERDIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>Café des sports</category><title>Ligue des nations : la France de Zinedine Zidane face à la montagne espagnole</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/caf%C3%A9-des-sports/20261120-ligue-nations-france-zinedine-zidane-face-montagne-espagnole</link><description>
La France affrontera l'Espagne en quarts de finale de la Ligue des nations, un défi XXL pour les Bleus face aux champions du monde en titre. Zinedine Zidane aura-t-il la recette pour enfin vaincre la "Roja" ?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/03f20e20-e512-11f1-82ed-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-7751560e.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/03f20e20-e512-11f1-82ed-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-7751560e.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">309226ec-e4ca-11f1-a4fd-3f9a4d954751</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 20:48:42 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Annie GASNIER</dc:creator></item><item><category>Une semaine dans le monde</category><title>Sommet de Shenzhen, guerre en Ukraine, hostilités dans le Golfe</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/une-semaine-dans-le-monde/20261120-sommet-de-shenzhen-guerre-en-ukraine-hostilit%C3%A9s-dans-le-golfe</link><description>

Pour la sixième semaine d'affilée, des syndicats, organisations de jeunesse et gilets jaunes appellent à protester samedi dans la rue contre la vie chère, dans un contexte de grogne sociale devenue européenne mais qui commence à se tasser les samedis en France. Les trois policiers ayant passé à tabac le producteur de musique noir Michel Zecler en 2020 ont été condamnés à des peines de un à deux ans de prison ferme. L'accusation avait de son côté requis, jeudi, entre quatre et six ans de prison ferme.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">844245cc-e52b-11f1-ab61-a5c9daa303ca</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 21:54:13 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg">© Benoit PEYRUCQ / AFP/Archives</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Au cœur de l’info, l’invité</category><title>Johann Chapoutot : "la dédiabolisation du RN est véritablement un mythe"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/au-c%C5%93ur-de-l-info-l-invit%C3%A9/20261120-johann-chapoutot-la-d%C3%A9diabolisation-du-rn-est-v%C3%A9ritablement-un-mythe</link><description>
A 5 mois de la présidentielle en France, le RN domine toujours dans les sondages. Longtemps considéré comme anti républicain, infréquentable, il est désormais aux portes du pouvoir. Comment comprendre cette progression? Quelle est la responsabilité de la classe politique dans cette évolution? Quelles conséquences sur notre démocratie? Johann Chapoutot, Professeur d'Histoire contemporaine, auteur de "La bascule, Allemagne 1933" (éditions Gallimard), était l'Invité d'Au Coeur de l'Info. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20054536-e522-11f1-9d9f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261120-200854-202823-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20054536-e522-11f1-9d9f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261120-200854-202823-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">141cd51a-e525-11f1-8891-754dc11be848</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 20:58:03 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Achren VERDIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Police : la loi sur la présomption de légitime défense définitivement adoptée par le Parlement</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-police-la-loi-sur-la-pr%C3%A9somption-de-l%C3%A9gitime-d%C3%A9fense-d%C3%A9finitivement-adopt%C3%A9e-par-le-parlement</link><description>
Vivement combattue dans la rue par ses opposants qui l'assimilent à un "permis de tuer", l'instauration d'une présomption d'usage légal des armes par les forces de l'ordre a été définitivement adoptée au Parlement vendredi soir, à la veille d'une nouvelle journée de mobilisation sociale.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ec88460c-e514-11f1-8bce-43bc8e8d3f8d</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 19:02:24 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg">© Geoffroy van der Hasselt, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fuites au ministère de l'Intérieur : comment le RN a progressivement séduit les hauts fonctionnaires</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-fuites-au-minist%C3%A8re-de-l-int%C3%A9rieur-comment-le-rn-a-progressivement-s%C3%A9duit-les-hauts-fonctionnaires</link><description>
Le parquet de Paris soupçonne l'ancien secrétaire général de Beauvau et actuel préfet du Loiret et de la région Centre-Val de Loire, Hugues Moutouh, d'avoir informé le Rassemblement national sur des enquêtes judiciaires visant le parti. Une affaire qui illustre l'influence grandissante du parti lepéniste dans les hautes sphères de l'État.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ed281fb0-e4ec-11f1-b121-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ed281fb0-e4ec-11f1-b121-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">845e625a-e4fb-11f1-8ece-9d792c6a9305</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:12:25 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ed281fb0-e4ec-11f1-b121-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg">© Pascal Guyot, AFP</source><dc:creator>Louis CHAHUNEAU</dc:creator></item><item><category>Outre-Mer</category><title>De l'océan Indien aux Caraïbes, la sécheresse frappe plusieurs territoires d'Outre-mer</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/outre-mer/20261120-de-l-oc%C3%A9an-indien-aux-cara%C3%AFbes-la-s%C3%A9cheresse-frappe-plusieurs-territoires-d-outre-mer</link><description>
La sécheresse s'installe durablement en Outre-mer. Le manque d'eau fragilise les cultures et menace les récoltes aux Antilles et à La Réunion. La situation est également très préoccupante en Guyane, où le niveau du fleuve continue de baisser.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d5ba9aa2-e4f5-11f1-a177-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-e00d5d0f.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d5ba9aa2-e4f5-11f1-a177-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-e00d5d0f.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">668bbe98-e4ca-11f1-b006-117a06c45e07</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:36:16 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator></dc:creator></item><item><category>ActuElles</category><title>Les féminicides, la partie émergée du contrôle coercitif</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/actuelles/20261120-les-f%C3%A9minicides-la-partie-%C3%A9merg%C3%A9e-du-contr%C3%B4le-coercitif</link><description>
Les féminicides font aussi des victimes invisibles : les proches des femmes assassinées, confrontées à un deuil impossible et à des embûches judiciaires. Dans 75 % des cas, le féminicide survient sans violences physiques préalables, mais au terme d'une période de contrôle coercitif :  une prison invisible faite d'emprise et de violences psychologiques, explique l'historienne Christelle Taraud, qui décrit des victimes "zombifiées" par leur tortionnaire.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/804fd37e-e4e7-11f1-94db-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/actuelles-4.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/804fd37e-e4e7-11f1-94db-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/actuelles-4.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">012b0ea0-e4e8-11f1-954f-b12e286687bf</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:46:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Laure MANENT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Gérard Depardieu et Michel Houellebecq accusés de viol en réunion et d'agressions sexuelles</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-g%C3%A9rard-depardieu-et-michel-houellebecq-accus%C3%A9s-de-viol-en-r%C3%A9union-et-d-agressions-sexuelles</link><description>
Gérard Depardieu est de nouveau accusé de viol – en réunion cette fois, avec la complicité supposée de l'écrivain Michel Houellebecq, selon des sources proches du dossier, confirmant vendredi des révélations de Mediapart. Les faits, dénoncés par une comédienne, remonteraient au tournage du film "Thalasso" en 2018.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/112bfeb0-e4f0-11f1-97c4-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/5b316d0d8e9e019339c005a7e2173a2aacfd39e4.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/112bfeb0-e4f0-11f1-97c4-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/5b316d0d8e9e019339c005a7e2173a2aacfd39e4.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">11ebaaf8-e4f0-11f1-af7a-57d065e8beab</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:38:36 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/112bfeb0-e4f0-11f1-97c4-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/5b316d0d8e9e019339c005a7e2173a2aacfd39e4.jpg">© Dimitar Dilkoff, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Dominique de Villepin annonce sa candidature à l'élection présidentielle de 2027</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261120-pr%C3%A9sidentielle-2027-l-ancien-premier-ministre-dominique-de-villepin-annonce-sa-candidature</link><description>
Dominique de Villepin a officialisé vendredi 20 novembre sa candidature à l'élection présidentielle de 2027. L'ex-Premier ministre se présente comme une alternative au macronisme, à La France insoumise et au Rassemblement national.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9fb85a8a-e4d6-11f1-8eb3-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/miniadefvillepin.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9fb85a8a-e4d6-11f1-8eb3-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/miniadefvillepin.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c6c746ae-e4d6-11f1-8ffb-375f4fe00708</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:42:32 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>La députée RN Laure Lavalette se défend d'être antisémite, se dédouane d'écrits vieux de "30 ans"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-accusations-antis%C3%A9mitisme-d%C3%A9put%C3%A9e-rn-laure-lavalette-invoque-faits-vieux-de-30-ans</link><description>
Selon une enquête publiée mercredi par le média Les Jours, la députée du Rassemblement national du Var Laure Lavalette aurait présidé, lors de ses années d'études, un syndicat étudiant dont la revue publiait des écrits antisémites. L'élue a balayé les accusations dans une interview sur BFMTV, arguant de faits vieux de "30 ans".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1684c9f4-e4bf-11f1-943c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-A49893B.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1684c9f4-e4bf-11f1-943c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-A49893B.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">00ba44a8-e4c1-11f1-9390-bd7bd8f937b3</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:26:06 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1684c9f4-e4bf-11f1-943c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-A49893B.jpg">© Miguel Medina, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Dominique de Villepin candidat : un homme de droite populaire à gauche mais en quête d'électeurs</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-france-presidentielle-2027-dominique-de-villepin-homme-droite-populaire-gauche-sans-electeurs</link><description>
L'ancien Premier ministre Dominique de Villepin a officialisé vendredi sa candidature à l'élection présidentielle de 2027. L'homme du "non" de la France à la guerre en Irak en 2003 est revenu sur le devant de la scène ces dernières années pour ses prises de position sur les sujets internationaux, en particulier sur la guerre à Gaza. Mais sa popularité est surtout marquée à gauche, au sein d'un électorat qui ne devrait pas voter pour lui.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fd73fc2c-e433-11f1-b4e5-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/main-Villepin.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fd73fc2c-e433-11f1-b4e5-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/main-Villepin.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c0ca20de-e434-11f1-a9ea-f369f859b733</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 06:43:38 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fd73fc2c-e433-11f1-b4e5-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/main-Villepin.png">© AFP / Studio graphique, FMM</source><dc:creator>Romain BRUNET</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Yannick Jadot claque la porte des Écologistes suite au rapprochement entre Marine Tondelier et LFI</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261119-france-presidentielle-yannick-jadot-quitte-les-ecologistes-marine-tondelier-jean-luc-melenchon-glucksmann</link><description>
Les fractures deviennent apparentes chez les Écologistes, au lendemain de la main tendue de Marine Tondelier à Jean-Luc Mélenchon : Yannick Jadot, sénateur et ex-candidat écologiste à la présidentielle, a annoncé qu'il quittait le parti, tout comme le député Jérémie Iordanoff. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2434c0c2-b5b2-11ec-ac2b-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/France-Elysee2022-YannickJadot.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2434c0c2-b5b2-11ec-ac2b-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/France-Elysee2022-YannickJadot.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">819cc766-e46d-11f1-9bfb-ffca175961e0</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 23:04:16 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2434c0c2-b5b2-11ec-ac2b-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/France-Elysee2022-YannickJadot.jpg">© Damien Meyer, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Politique</category><title>Présidentielle 2027 : primaire de la droite et du centre, Marine Tondelier tend la main à LFI</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/politique/20261119-pr%C3%A9sidentielle-2027-primaire-de-la-droite-et-du-centre-marine-tondelier-tend-la-main-%C3%A0-lfi</link><description>
